queries: WITH g AS (SELECT p.fundflux AS fundflux, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) AS n FROM scanqc q JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = q.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux) SELECT fundflux, n AS project_count, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, n * 1.0 / AVG(n * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_average FROM g

assumptions.assumption: Projects with a NULL fundflux form a single group of their own; GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group, so no extra handling is needed. Empty-string funding values stay separate groups.
The total and the average per funding source are taken over the groups that have at least one QC-linked project (inner join).
Values are left unrounded, with multiplication by 1.0 to force non-integer division.

responses.sql: SELECT fundflux AS funding_source, project_count, project_count * 1.0 / SUM(project_count) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, project_count * 1.0 / AVG(project_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_average FROM (SELECT p.fundflux, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) AS project_count FROM scanqc q JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = q.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux) t ORDER BY funding_source;

assumptions.assumption: A missing funding source means NULL fundflux. GROUP BY puts all NULLs in one group, and that group is reported with a NULL funding_source. Empty strings are not treated as missing.

The average per funding source is the mean of the project counts across the funding-source groups that have at least one project with QC records, including the NULL group. It is not averaged over all funding sources in projects.
The fraction and ratio are left unrounded. They are computed with decimal arithmetic (multiplying by 1.0) to avoid integer division.

assumptions.assumption: Projects with a NULL fundflux form one group (GROUP BY puts NULLs together). Empty-string funding values are left as their own group, not merged with NULL.
The average per funding source is the mean of the per-group distinct project counts, taken across the groups that have QC records (including the NULL group).
Values are left unrounded and the multiplication by 1.0 forces non-integer division.
